Four corrections are required:

1. The initially classified custody is not retained. durable_lifecycle.py:462–482 stores only the Boolean classification, profile, full permit and module. adapter:767–775 validates the current initial custody but returns only True. Both later validators look up _CONTROLLER_STARTUPS again (adapter:635–640 and721–726), accepting the custody currently there. A same-type replacement after consumption, preserving the startup, consumed session, referenced records and snapshots, is checked against its own fields rather than the initially classified custody. The existing snapshot functions do not contain the custody object's identity. Therefore the specified substitution refusal is missing even though simple deletion of _CONTROLLER_STARTUPS would refuse. Retain the exact initial custody and corresponding record/token/owner binding in fixed internal attempt data, and compare that same object and current issuance at both boundaries. Do not replace these checks with equality of copied fields. A source-level negative should replace the custody through a bounded inert lower hook after actual issuance and require refusal before resume/publication; this is not an observed native exploit.

2. The fixed validator functions are not retained. durable_lifecycle.py:502 and560 perform fresh attribute lookups on the retained module. Changing _validate_controller_pre_resume or _validate_controller_worker_stage during an inert create/bind/finish hook therefore changes the callable used by the new boundary. In particular, a finish hook can change the selected configuration and replace the stage helper; the factory then invokes that replacement immediately before publishing. The canonical brief specifically requires fixed helpers bound outside locks and retained for the attempt. Capture those original functions internally and refuse changed bindings as appropriate; do not accept a supplied module or generic callback. Merely retaining the module object does not retain its attributes. This is a failure of the stated local fixed-call contract, not a claim that arbitrary Python mutation is an operating-system authority boundary.

3. The kernel exposes an unchecked optional attempt path. durable_lifecycle.py:538–546 accepts any non-None attempt, stores it in _attempts, and otherwise retrieves an entry that may be absent. Lines559–563 either call attempt.adapter's method under the state locks or skip the controller check. There is no exact attempt type, factory issuance, same startup/full permit/raw permit, owner, record or module binding check before create. A caller-provided object with is_controller=False suppresses the pre-resume check; one with is_controller=True selects a method-bearing object. The ordinary factory currently supplies its own newly created record, so this review does not claim that its normal call automatically takes that bypass. It is nevertheless the optional caller-selected checking path forbidden by the brief and leaves direct internal entry unable to enforce the new controller relation. Make any connecting attempt data mandatory and factory-owned/identity-checked for a controller start, preserve the old public/delegate signatures, and refuse missing/substituted data before lower effects. No optional validator or caller-controlled module belongs in this seam. Also verify the initially issued controller permit cannot be reclassified as generated when its candidate profile changes.

4. The supplied adapter diff is not a valid complete unified patch. My passive checker8a07a3 exited1 at asr_loading_adapter.diff line9: an unprefixed empty body line, with malformed context already visible around lines5–7. It cannot reconstruct either direction as supplied. The durable diff does reconstruct the entire LF-normalized before/after pair in both directions. The adapter source itself preserves the exact34,968-byte accepted prefix. Preserve the malformed diff and regenerate a separate exact mechanical diff after the source corrections; do not silently repair whitespace in this original. Plain before/name -> name headers require zero path stripping for those literal names; strip semantics do not repair this malformed body.

The placement and ordinary cleanup are otherwise consistent with the narrow direction. The canonical adapter import is outside the state locks. The new pre-resume helper checks the distinct WORKER_BOUND / resume_attempted=False / unpublished session state without changing the accepted stage predicate. It checks consumed startup, current selection, permit/record/protection, live token and retained _starts/token worker. The factory uses finish_start, not published, immediately before its assignments. The actual lock order is manager then token; bind_worker and finish_start remain outside those locks. resume_owned sets its attempt flag only after the new pre-resume check and retains its existing single-resume rule.

The existing returned-worker cleanup paths are preserved. A kernel check failure retains _starts and attempts exact stop while preserving its original error; the factory assignment has not completed, so it does not add a second stop for that path. A final factory check failure uses the returned local worker even though owner._worker is still None, then quarantines and re-raises. The real _fixed_real_worker_start remains unconditionally closed after validation, and the generated delegate source bytes were not changed. I do not infer successful generated compatibility or test reachability from those facts; root and the other peer own the fixture/test review.

# Final fixture/test source findings — 2026-09-14

The fixture and ten proposed cases need correction before qualification. These are source findings, not observed test failures. The three one-time worker snapshots match the final frozen delivery byte for byte; passive check `7cfd95` exited 0 and confirms all ten IDs in source order. Only this unchanged fixture/test review is upgraded from preliminary to final. This is not a complete core-source verdict.

Bindings: fixture `e9229f73dc8d004a71a6c45f73cae7e57985cf3458ca00a96dbb2120bcfbf215`; tests `b2c4b52127e3a51a43b05367124993c0bb4ed1f621b7eab20d63ac5d97113511`; EXPECTED `401a3149a38ca03fc49ea150575340318e736b612c3941539a7c6d8b8c2e58f0`. 1. **The generated-gate case does not exercise that gate.** Test lines 190–201 pass `object()` through inherited `Kernel.create_suspended`, which ignores the profile (donor test_reservations.py:544–547). There is no wrong-profile refusal assertion and neither new file imports either generated flow. The actual gates are generated_adapter_flow.py:764–784 (exact _OwnedASRStart/binding) and generated_worker_flow.py:132–135 (internal sentinel). Use these actual gates over inert lower services for the required positive and refusal controls.

2. **Worker substitution occurs before the intended boundary.** Fixture lines 84–88 call `on_created` before returning the worker. Current durable_lifecycle.py:551 then overwrites the test's `_starts` replacement. The token-worker replacement instead violates the existing `token.worker is None` condition in snapshot_reservations.py:349–350, before the new validator. The owner replacement reaches `record.owner._revoked` at durable:557 with a bare object, before exact-owner validation. These cases do not isolate the advertised post-binding/pre-resume checks. Move the negative mutations to an inert seam after actual binding while preserving the actual validator and stop path.

3. **The secondary-cleanup failure is armed too early.** Test line 125 installs unconditional sync failure before entering `f.scope()`. The fresh journal's INITIALIZED append calls the same sync function during lease entry (reservations:260; file port:68; donor fixture:49–51). Thus the failure variants cannot establish the intended boundary revocation, first SessionClosed error or one exact worker stop. Arm the failure only after the primary boundary event. The nonfailure branches merely set `_revoked`; none exits the lease at that boundary, and no assertion compares the original exception object or retained custody/worker identities after cleanup uncertainty.

4. **Required custody/helper replacement coverage is missing.** Test lines 176–188 only delete one registry entry, despite its “substituted” name. No case replaces matching custody, either fixed validator, or the canonical module/class binding. This matters for the current factory: its attempt retains a boolean and module (durable:462–467), then looks up validators from that module (502, 560). Tests should expose replacement after classification and require the captured exact authority or refusal, without installing permissive validators as positive authority. The optional `attempt=None` signature at 538 also has no contract-preservation check.

5. **Success-fixture cleanup is skipped on an assertion failure.** In fixture:185–194, close/join follows `yield` without `finally`. An exception in the positive test skips that explicit close/join; only the surrounding scope's quarantine path remains. The test makes no assertion about the exact retained worker or custody on this path. Make failure teardown explicit while preserving the first error and retained uncertain custody. This is an inert-fixture gap, not a measured native leak.

The positive source does use canonical imports, actual startup issuance, actual consumption, actual factory entry and ordinary bind/resume; I found no positive registry seeding or substituted validator. Temporary globals restore through ExitStack, and the closed real-worker test calls the actual entry. Those useful properties do not fill the gaps above.
